territorial_scope.description: Applies to New Mexico state elections under the Campaign Reporting Act; excludes federal, municipal, school board and special district elections.

evidence.quote: any primary, general or statewide special election in New Mexico

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Amends New Mexico's Campaign Reporting Act to require AI disclaimers on ads containing materially deceptive media and to bar distributing such media within ninety days before an election with intent to mislead voters; violations carry civil penalties or crimes. The text states no effective date.
summary.long: The act amends the Campaign Reporting Act and adds §1-19-26.8. It defines artificial intelligence and materially deceptive media (an image, video or audio depicting an individual in conduct or speech they did not engage in, published without consent and produced in whole or part using AI). Section 2 requires advertisements with expenditures above $1,000 to name the candidate, committee or person who authorized and paid for them. Advertisements containing materially deceptive media must carry a disclaimer that the media has been manipulated or generated by artificial intelligence, with prominence and duration rules; each non-compliant occurrence is a separate violation subject to civil penalties under §1-19-34.6. Exemptions cover certain broadcasters, satire, and distribution platforms with consistent disclaimer requirements. Section 3 prohibits distributing, or agreeing with another person to distribute, materially deceptive media within ninety days before an election, where the person knows it falsely represents a depicted individual and intends to mislead electors, unless a disclaimer is included. Willful and knowing violations are a misdemeanor for a first conviction and a fourth-degree felony for a second. Enforcement may be sought by the attorney general, a district attorney, a depicted individual, an injured candidate or an organization representing voters.

notes: The text states no effective date or emergency clause, so none is coded. Section 2 subsection D requires disclaimers on any advertisement containing materially deceptive media, without the election-window or intent conditions that Section 3 subsection A attaches to distribution; the two provisions differ in scope. Penalty amounts are not stated in this text. Section 3 subsection E gives enforcement standing to private persons (depicted individuals, candidates, organizations), and Section 2 subsection H and Section 3 subsection F preserve other civil claims.

"artificial intelligence" means a machine-based or computer-based system that through hardware or software uses input data to emulate the structure and characteristics of input data in order to generate synthetic content, including images, video or audio
"depicted individual" means an individual whose image, photo, likeness or voice is represented in an advertisement or other media in such a manner that results in the individual being identifiable

"distribution platform" means a website, internet forum or message board, application or a published newspaper, magazine or other periodical of general circulation, including an internet or electronic publication, that carries news and commentary
"materially deceptive media" means an image, video or audio that: (1) depicts an individual engaged in conduct or speech in which the depicted individual did not engage;

obligations.summary: Persons making campaign, coordinated or independent expenditures above $1,000 (per advertisement, or aggregated per cycle) must ensure the advertisement names the candidate, committee or person who authorized and paid for it; disclaimers must be legible on visual media and clearly spoken on audio media.
obligations.conditional_on: Expenditure for an advertisement exceeding $1,000 alone or aggregated with the same person's advertisement expenditures in the election cycle; exemptions in Subsection B for small items and impracticable media.

evidence.quote: shall ensure that the advertisement contains the name of the candidate, committee or other person who authorized and paid for the advertisement.

obligations.summary: A person who creates, produces or purchases an advertisement containing materially deceptive media must include a clear and conspicuous disclaimer in every language used, stating that the image, video or audio has been manipulated or generated by artificial intelligence; Subsection E sets size, duration and audio-spacing rules for the disclaimer.
obligations.conditional_on: The advertisement contains materially deceptive media as defined in NMSA 1-19-26(S).

evidence.quote: the advertisement shall include a disclaimer.

obligations.summary: Any person (individual or entity) may not distribute, or enter into an agreement with another person to distribute, materially deceptive media when the person knows it falsely represents a depicted individual, the distribution occurs within ninety days before an election, and the person intends and is reasonably likely to alter electors' voting behavior by misleading them; the prohibition is subject to the disclaimer exception in Subsection B.
obligations.conditional_on: Distribution within ninety days before an election; knowledge of false representation; intent to alter voting behavior; reasonably likely to cause that result; no applicable disclaimer under Subsection B.

evidence.quote: it is a violation of the Campaign Reporting Act for a person to distribute or enter into an agreement with another person to distribute materially deceptive media

obligations.summary: To fall outside the prohibition in Subsection A, materially deceptive media must include a clear and conspicuous disclaimer in every language used, stating that the image, video or audio has been manipulated or generated by artificial intelligence; Subsection C sets the form of the disclaimer for image, video, audio and mixed media.
obligations.conditional_on: Relevant only to materially deceptive media distributed in the Subsection A circumstances; the disclaimer is a condition of the exception.

evidence.quote: that media includes a disclaimer that appears in a clear and conspicuous manner in every language used in the media
